properties.natural_language: All incoming P2P gossip messages must be encoded with the correct fork version corresponding to the current epoch. Messages with fork versions that do not match the expected version for the current epoch must be rejected.
The fork version computation must check epoch thresholds in strict descending order to ensure the most recent applicable fork version is always selected.
The P2P fork version used for message encoding must always correspond to a valid, recognized fork. Unknown or undefined fork versions must never be used for encoding or accepted during decoding.
Before a fork epoch boundary, all network participants must be running software that recognizes the new fork version. The fork activation mechanism assumes coordinated network upgrade.
After the epoch boundary check determines the fork is active, the system must transition to the EIP-7928 fork state and all subsequent P2P messages must use the EIP-7928 fork version.
Contract creation transactions must have initcode size <= 49152 bytes (MAX_INITCODE_SIZE). Transactions exceeding this limit must be rejected before any execution.
The initcode must be extracted from the transaction data field before size validation. The extraction must correctly identify the initcode portion for contract creation transactions.
After initcode gas cost calculation, the intrinsic gas must include INITCODE_WORD_COST (2) * ceil(len(initcode) / 32) additional gas. The total intrinsic gas must reflect this added cost.
The transaction gas limit must be >= intrinsic gas (including initcode cost). If insufficient, the transaction must be rejected with no state changes.
During CREATE/CREATE2 execution, initcode read from memory must not exceed MAX_INITCODE_SIZE (49152 bytes). Exceeding this limit must trigger an exceptional abort that consumes all remaining gas.
After successful initcode size validation during CREATE/CREATE2, the initcode gas cost must be charged and the contract address computed before initcode execution begins.

The initcode gas metering must ensure that the cost of jumpdest analysis is always proportional to initcode size. Post-EIP-3860, the minimum gas cost for maximum-sized initcode must be high enough to prevent DoS via jumpdest analysis attacks.
Initcode size validation must occur before initcode gas metering. The size check must precede the gas cost calculation to prevent gas charges on oversized initcode that will be rejected.
If EOF containers are present, the initcode size limit of 49152 bytes must still apply to the total initcode payload including any EOF-specific headers and sections.
All bitwise operations (AND, OR, XOR, NOT, SHL, SHR, SAR, BYTE) must operate on unsigned 256-bit integers (U256). Operands must always be within [0, 2^256 - 1] and results must be modulo 2^256.
Before executing any bitwise operation, the stack must contain sufficient operands (2 for binary ops, 1 for NOT). If the stack has insufficient items, a stack underflow exception must occur.
All bitwise operations must consume exactly GAS_VERY_LOW (3) gas. Gas must be charged after operands are popped but before execution.
After any bitwise operation completes successfully, exactly one result must be pushed to the stack and the program counter must be incremented by 1.

For SHL and SHR operations, if the shift amount >= 256, the result must be zero. For SAR with shift >= 256, the result must be 0 if the value is non-negative, or MAX_UINT256 if the value is negative (sign-extended).
AND(a,b) must equal bitwise a & b; OR(a,b) must equal a | b; XOR(a,b) must equal a ^ b; NOT(a) must equal bitwise complement (~a) within U256 (equivalent to MAX_UINT256 - a).
BYTE(i, x) must return the i-th byte of x in big-endian order (byte 0 is the most significant). If i >= 32, the result must be 0.
All bitwise operations must have constant gas cost regardless of operand values, preventing timing-based side channels that could leak information about operand contents.

When a Type 3 (blob) transaction is received from a peer, the transaction metadata must be accepted without blob sidecars. The node must extract versioned hashes (vhashes) to request blobs separately.
Blob data received via PooledBlobs messages must have their versioned hashes validated against the originally requested vhashes. Missing or hash-mismatched blobs must be rejected.
A node MUST NOT forward a blob transaction to other peers until ALL blobs referenced by the transaction have been received and validated. Partial blob sets must block forwarding.
Failed blob validation must also block transaction forwarding. Both incomplete and invalid blob sets must prevent the transaction from being propagated.
After extracting vhashes, a GetPooledBlobs request must be constructed containing exactly the versioned hashes from the transaction and sent to an appropriate peer.
Upon receiving a GetPooledBlobs request, the node must look up requested blobs in its pool and return a PooledBlobs response containing found blobs. Missing blobs may be omitted from the response.
After all blobs are validated, the transaction must transition to ready-to-forward state and may be propagated to peers with full blob sidecars.
Error handling for GetPooledBlobs requests with unknown vhashes must be defined. Peers must not be disconnected for requesting blobs that have already been pruned from the pool.

The vhash enumeration in a blob transaction must not allow an observer to determine which blobs belong to which transaction without possessing the transaction itself, preserving transaction privacy during the two-phase fetch.
New consensus feature specifications must pass the linter validation before being integrated into the build system. Linter failures must block further integration steps.
After successful linter validation and builder registration, CI tests must be executed. Only specifications that pass all CI tests are considered integration-ready.
During fork transition, new BeaconState fields must be initialized to their default values. After initialization, the state must be in a valid post-fork configuration with all new fields present.
The relay must return a valid, highest-value bid header in response to getHeader requests. If the relay is unresponsive, the proposer must fall back to local block building to avoid missing the slot.
Builder bid payloads must be validated by the relay before presentation to proposers. Invalid payloads, censored blocks, or undervalued bids must be filtered by relay validation.
Searcher transaction bundles are untrusted. Standard transaction validation must apply to all individual transactions within bundles before inclusion in builder blocks.

After a proposer signs a blinded block header and submits it to the relay, the proposer is irrevocably committed. The relay must then reveal the full execution payload. Failure to reveal results in a missed slot.
A proposer must be registered via registerValidator before participating in the builder auction. Unregistered proposers must not receive bid headers.

The proposer-builder separation trust model relies on the relay as a trusted intermediary. If the relay is compromised or a builder submits a malicious payload, the proposer's commitment (signed blinded block) cannot be revoked, creating a liveness risk.

After the relay selects the highest bid, the proposer must receive payment at least equal to the bid value upon successful block inclusion. MEV extraction revenue must flow from searcher bundles through builders to proposers.

The CL must independently validate parent_hash consistency, RANDAO mix, timestamp ordering, and the no-empty-transactions constraint before delegating full execution validation to the EL via Engine API.

Proposed beacon blocks must pass full validation including execution payload checks and signature verification. Equivocating proposers (signing two different blocks for the same slot) must be slashed.

Slashing evidence (ProposerSlashing/AttesterSlashing) must be cryptographically verified with conflicting signatures from the same validator. Reporter identity is irrelevant; evidence validity is independently verifiable.
The merge transition is irreversible: once is_merge_transition_complete returns true, the system must never re-enter the pre-merge state. All subsequent blocks must contain valid execution payloads.

After the merge transition block is processed (first block where execution_enabled is true and merge is not yet complete), the system must transition to post-merge state with execution payload validation permanently enabled.

After slashing a validator, the validator's effective balance must be reduced by at least 1/MIN_SLASHING_PENALTY_QUOTIENT_BELLATRIX (1/32). The validator's withdrawable epoch must be set and the slashed flag must be true.
RANDAO processing must occur after parent hash validation but before timestamp validation. The ordering of validation steps must be deterministic across all implementations.
Input to the secp256r1 precompile (0x100) must be exactly 160 bytes. Inputs of any other length must result in an empty return value (verification failure) with gas still consumed.
Signature components r and s must satisfy 0 < r < n and 0 < s < n where n is the secp256r1 curve order. Values outside these bounds must cause verification failure.
Public key coordinates qx and qy must satisfy 0 <= qx < p and 0 <= qy < p where p is the field prime. The point (qx, qy) must lie on the secp256r1 curve and must not be the point at infinity.

The precompile must always consume exactly 6900 gas regardless of whether verification succeeds or fails. Gas must be charged before any validation logic executes. The precompile must never revert - it returns empty bytes on failure.
On successful signature verification, the precompile must return a 32-byte value of 0x01 (left-padded). On failure, it must return empty bytes (zero-length).

The precompile accepts malleable signatures: both (r, s) and (r, n-s) are valid for the same message and public key. Applications requiring non-malleability must implement their own s-value canonicalization.

All untrusted external signature data entering via WebAuthn/FIDO2 devices must pass through the full validation pipeline: format check (160 bytes), cryptographic bounds checks (r, s, qx, qy), curve membership, and non-identity verification before the ECDSA algorithm is executed.
The trie root hash must be deterministic: given the same set of key-value pairs, the computed Merkle root must always be identical regardless of insertion order.
An empty trie must always produce the EMPTY_TRIE_ROOT constant (keccak256 of RLP-encoded empty string). This value must be consistent across all implementations.
After a trie_set operation, the key-value pair must be retrievable via trie_get. The trie must transition from empty to populated state on first insertion.
When encoding trie nodes, if the RLP-encoded node is >= 32 bytes, it must be stored by its keccak256 hash (hash reference). If < 32 bytes, it must be inlined directly in the parent node.
After internal node encoding, if an invalid node type is encountered or root computation fails, an encoding error state must be reached. No partial or corrupted root hash may be returned.
For secured tries (account/storage), all keys must be hashed with keccak256 before trie insertion to prevent trie balancing attacks. The secured flag must determine whether key hashing is applied.
After key processing, keys must be converted to nibble sequences (4-bit units) for trie traversal, and then compact-encoded for storage in leaf and extension nodes.
Trie copy operations must produce a deep copy (frozen dataclass semantics). Modifications to the copied trie must not affect the original trie's state or root hash.

At block number 2,675,000 on mainnet, the Spurious Dragon fork must activate, enabling EIP-155 (replay protection), EIP-160 (EXP cost), EIP-161 (state clearing), and EIP-170 (code size limit) simultaneously.
Post-Spurious Dragon, all transactions must include a valid chain ID per EIP-155. Transactions with mismatched chain IDs (replay attacks from other chains) must be rejected.
After the fork block is reached, all four EIPs (155, 160, 161, 170) must be activated atomically. No partial activation is permitted.
After a transaction touches an account, if the account is empty (zero nonce, zero balance, no code), it must be removed from the state trie per EIP-161.
